title: Renewables Power the Orbit? Achieving Sustainable Space Edge Computing via QoS-Aware Offloading.
abstract: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations are becoming integral to 6G infrastructure, but increasing in-orbit computation accelerates battery degradation and raises sustainability concerns. Meanwhile, renewable-heavy regions worldwide experience persistent energy curtailment due to transmission bottlenecks, leaving substantial clean energy stranded near generation sites. We identify a satellite-grid co-design opportunity: adaptively offloading task-critical data from satellite to data centers co-located with renewable power plants. However, realizing this vision requires jointly considering intermittent and capacity-limited communication windows, as well as time-varying electricity budgets. In this paper, we propose SQSO, a Sustainable and QoS-aware Satellite Offloading framework that models per-interval task offloading as a constrained optimization over dynamic topology and electricity prices. Under this framework, we design $\text{AO}^2$, an adaptive offloading orchestration algorithm to solve the formulated optimization problem. Using Starlink-scale simulations and real-world electricity price traces, $\text{AO}^2$ reduces energy consumption by up to 76.03% and battery life consumption by up to 76.85% compared to state-of-the-art schemes, while also lowering task delay. This work highlights that sustainable scaling of LEO constellations requires co-design of space networking and renewable energy infrastructure, while our solution promotes renewable-aware task offloading and cross-domain collaboration for space-energy integration in the 6G era.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: NeuroForensics: Unmasking Covert Backdoor Attack via Endogenous Defense.
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates decentralized training without exchanging raw data, yet remains inherently susceptible to backdoor attacks. Existing defenses predominantly rely on statistical outlier detection, assumed that malicious updates exhibit significant deviations from benign ones. However, this premise is fundamentally flawed in real-world scenarios, particularly against covert backdoor attacks within non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data conditions. In this paper, we propose a robust FL defense framework, called NeuroForensics, that employs a target-oriented approach to resist covert backdoor attacks under Non-IID data characteristics. To uncover endogenous anomalies, we project high-dimensional model weights into a Posterior Probability Matrix via Pseudo Feature Vectors (PFV). This projection helps magnify the endogenous divergences between malicious and benign clients. Furthermore, to characterize these disparities across multiple dimensions, we incorporate a multi-metric fusion strategy that synthesizes matrix features into a unified anomaly detection score, enabling an adaptive thresholding mechanism to accurately isolate malicious clients. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that NeuroForensics significantly outperforms existing defense schemes, suppressing backdoor success rates while preserving high main-task utility, even under covert attacks and extreme Non-IID conditions.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Toward Communication-Sensing Integrated Cloud-Network Monitoring: Real-Time Vibration Event Recognition on Underground Optical Cables.
abstract: Underground optical cables are key assets in cloudnetwork infrastructure, and distributed optical fiber sensing enables them to serve as both communication media and sensing resources for external disturbance monitoring. This paper presents a real-time vibration event recognition framework for communication-sensing integrated underground opticalcable monitoring based on $\Phi$-OTDR signals. To avoid temporal information leakage, continuous vibration traces are divided into non-overlapping training, validation, and testing periods before sliding-window segmentation and Z-score standardization. The proposed SE-DMRCB model integrates parallel multiscale 1D convolutions, stacked residual blocks, and squeezeand-excitation attention to capture both impulsive and periodic vibration patterns. Bayesian optimization is employed to select key hyperparameters for balancing recognition accuracy and model complexity. Experiments on a real-world underground optical-cable deployment with eight vibration-event categories show that the proposed method achieves 99.84% test accuracy with an end-to-end recognition latency of 10.55 ms per window, which is much lower than the 512 ms window-update interval. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can support online recognition and sensing-assisted diagnosis for cloud-network infrastructure operation.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Temporal Predictive Joint Hybrid Beamforming Framework for Mitigating Channel Aging in High-Mobility MIMO-OFDM Systems.
abstract: As a key technology for enhancing spectral efficiency, Frequency Division Duplexing (FDD) massive multipleinput multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) is limited by channel aging in high-mobility scenarios. The latency in channel estimation and feedback renders Base Station (BS) CSI outdated relative to rapid channel variations caused by Doppler shifts, leading to beam misalignment. To combat the issue, we propose a unified framework called Predictive Attention-aided Multi-Scale Hybrid Beamforming (PAMS-HBF). The architecture integrates a Learnable Pilot Sensing (LPS) module for adaptive downlink pilot design, functioning for both downlink pilot transmission and user-side pilot sensing, alongside a Long Short-Term Channel Prediction (LSTCP) module using LSTM to forecast CSI for aging compensation. A Multi-Scale CSI Feedback (MCF) module employs multi-scale convolutions to capture diverse features for compression. An Efficient Channel Attention Beamforming (ECAB) module at the BS reconstructs features to generate beamforming matrices. Experimental results demonstrate that PAMS-HBF maintains consistent performance across different velocities. Comparisons show its superiority over traditional algorithms and static deep learning schemes. The proposed method at sufficient feedback bits exceeds the lossless feedback baseline by approximately 23.1%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Tremerity-Fi: Non-Contact Daily-Life Tremor Severity Assessment by Commercial mmWave Radar.
abstract: Tremor is a common symptom of neurological diseases. The regular assessment of daily tremors facilitates the evaluation of disease progression and assists clinicians in optimizing treatment strategies. However, current home monitoring solutions have difficulty in dealing with user cooperation, privacy concerns, environmental interference, and system generalization, leading to feasibility concerns in activities of daily living (ADL). To this end, we propose Tremerity-Fi, a non-contact and privacy-friendly tremor severity assessment system based on mmWave radar. To realize Tremerity-Fi, we first design an adaptive beamforming algorithm to accurately identify useful but weak signals from numerous reflections captured in the environment. Second, unlike primary reflections commonly used in mmWave sensing, we leverage multipath reflections that carry useful information about the target's motion, even though they are generally considered harmful, to help reconstruct hand signals and improve sensing performance. Furthermore, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation algorithm to improve the ability to adapt to unseen environments and users. We collect a diverse dataset of 5 patients and 25 healthy subjects in 3 scenarios, such as offices, homes, and hospitals. Extensive experiments show that our system achieves 94.51% accuracy in tremor detection, about 5 higher than the SOTA mmWave radar method, and 89.13% in tremor severity assessment, demonstrating its sufficient potential as a tremor monitoring assistant for patients with neurological diseases.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Joint Optimization of Video Recommendation and Cooperative Edge Caching for Maximizing Profit.
abstract: The rapid growth of multi-version video-on-demand (VoD) services places increasing pressure on mobile networks. Edge caching offers a promising solution by bringing content closer to mobile users (MUs). However, practical edge caching systems face a fundamental challenge: MUs exhibit highly varied preferences across video contents and bitrates, whereas edge resources are limited, costly, and influenced by pricing decisions from mobile network operators (MNOs). In this paper, we study a novel, profit-oriented joint optimization problem that integrates personalized video recommendation, cooperative multi-version edge caching, soft cache hits, and economic incentives. We model the interaction between the MNO and the video provider (VP) as a Stackelberg game, which explicitly captures the coupling between pricing decisions, caching strategies, and various demands of MUs. We also show that the studied problem is NP-hard due to its non-convex structure and the presence of mixed discrete-continuous decision variables. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Backward-Induction Stackelberg framework, in which the MNO optimizes cache-leasing prices via an iterative distance-weighted strategy, while the VP solves its NP-hard joint decision problem through block coordinate descent combined with relaxation-and-rounding techniques. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art schemes, improving the MNO’s revenue by up to 32.18% and the VP’s revenue by up to 33.43%, while remaining robust under diverse system configurations.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CF-BAD: Coarse-to-Fine Granularity BGP Anomaly Detection for Prefix Hijacking.
abstract: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) serves as the defacto standard for inter-domain routing, yet it fundamentally lacks authentication and validation mechanisms, leaving the global Internet infrastructure vulnerable to both malicious attacks and inadvertent misconfigurations. Traditional detection approaches often fall short in accurately identifying prefix hijacking, particularly in small-scale events, and typically produce results that are difficult to interpret. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CF-BAD, a novel anomaly detection framework. Specifically, to capture the subtle patterns characteristic of small-scale anomalies, we construct a dual-granular feature tensor that integrates both time- and frequency-domain information derived from raw BGP data. We further introduce an adaptive mask mechanism tailored for the Swin-Transformer architecture, enabling enhanced representation learning across both coarse- and fine-grained knowledge. Our detection model also incorporates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) unit to effectively capture long- and short-term temporal dependencies. To improve interpretability, we devise a novel layer-wise root cause analysis (RCA) method that provides explainable insights via hierarchical decomposition. Extensive experiments conducted on 15 real-world anomaly events comprising 343 million BGP messages in total demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in both detection and RCA accuracy across the majority of cases.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: The Imitation Game: Using Large Language Models to Disrupt Chinese Chat-Based Cybercrime.
abstract: Chat-based cybercrime has emerged as a pervasive threat, with attackers leveraging real-time messaging platforms to conduct scams that rely on trust-building, deception, and psychological manipulation. Traditional defense mechanisms, which operate on static rules or shallow content filters, struggle to identify these conversational threats, especially when attackers use multimedia obfuscation and context-aware dialogue. In this work, we ask a provocative question inspired by the classic Imitation Game: Can machines convincingly pose as human victims to turn deception against cybercriminals? We present LURE (LLM-based User Response Engagement), the first system to deploy Large Language Models (LLMs) as active agents (not as passive classifiers) embedded within adversarial chat environments. LURE combines automated discovery, adversarial interaction, and OCR-based analysis of image-embedded payment data. Applied to the setting of Chinese illicit video chat scams on Telegram, our system engaged 53 actors across 98 groups. In over 56% of interactions, the LLM maintained multi-round conversations without being noticed as a bot, effectively “winning” the imitation game. Our findings reveal key behavioral patterns in scam operations, such as payment flows, upselling strategies, and platform migration tactics.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Beagle: Auto-tuning Performance Diagnosis for Live Video Streaming.
abstract: Delivering high-quality live video to millions of users is challenging, and performance can be impacted by a wide range of components in the ecosystem (e.g., CDNs, ISPs, protocols) as well as how these components interact with each other. In this paper, our primary contribution is Beagle, a novel system for root-causing performance anomalies in the video streaming context. As part of Beagle, we developed custom interpretable ML models based on mechanisms used by domain experts (e.g., filters based on rules and a graph relating those rules). Leveraging pre-training and few-shot learning, Beagle supports automatic learning and adaptation of rule thresholds and graph relationships from limited ground truth information. Evaluations with real-world dataset of live streaming sessions from a popular streaming service show (i) Beagle significantly outperforms alternatives including Gradient Boosted Decision Trees, and a Deep Neural Network approach; and (ii) Beagle is effective in auto-tuning production expert designed system for root cause identification. Even with less than ten root causes to learn from, Beagle reduces the Mistake Rate made by expert configured rules by nearly an order of magnitude.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Odysseus: A Context-Level Pre-training Framework for Out-of-Distribution Encrypted Traffic Classification.
abstract: Encrypted traffic classification is essential for network security, management, and Quality of Service (QoS), but models trained under IID assumptions often degrade after deployment due to application updates, temporal drift, and infrastructural changes. We observe that short-window multi-flow context provides more stable behavioral cues than isolated flows, while self-supervised pre-training can learn transferable priors from unlabeled traffic without target-domain labels. We present Odysseus, a context-level pre-training framework for OOD encrypted traffic classification. Odysseus converts raw pcaps into a Multi-Scale Flow Grid Representation (MSFGR) and pre-trains a masked autoencoder with complementary packet- and flow-level masking to capture intra-/inter-flow structure. During fine-tuning, it integrates Hierarchical Attention Distillation (HAD), Traffic-Aware Augmentation and Contrastive Learning (TACL), and Associated Flow Prediction (AFP) to enhance context modeling, distill context knowledge into a deployable flow-level branch, and regularize OOD-robust relational representations. Across 11 scenarios (5 IID, 6 OOD) spanning Cross-Version, Cross-Time, Cross-Spatiotemporal, and Cross-Type shifts, Odysseus achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves OOD F1-Score by up to $15.70\%$, reaching $85.38\%$, $90.05\%$, $71.93\%$, and $99.62/96.87/72.55\%$ F1 on the corresponding OOD settings. Further analyses confirm the effectiveness of each component, strong few-shot robustness, graceful degradation under noisy/missing context, and advantages over matrix-based inputs.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Privacy-aware Hand Gesture Recognition using Textile-based Sensing Glove.
abstract: Gesture recognition using a wearable sensor glove enables intuitive human-robot interaction, virtual reality, and rehabilitation systems; however, hand motion patterns and finger configurations are highly user-specific and may reveal sensitive biometric information. To address this issue, this study implements a federated learning-based gesture recognition framework utilizing a textile-based sensing glove. In this study, multichannel signals from five finger sensors embedded in the glove were processed. A lightweight Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) temporal model was employed, and two federated learning strategies, Federated Averaging (FedAvg) and Federated Representation (FedRep), were implemented. Using centralized training, the model achieved accuracies of 99.78% and 75.87% under random split and Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) evaluation, whereas using federated training, accuracies of 99.81% and 75.06% were obtained, respectively. As a result, it has been shown that federated learning preserves recognition performance with only a slight reduction in accuracy while providing improved data privacy. The findings demonstrate that combining temporal modeling with personalized federated learning enables privacyaware and low-latency gesture recognition suitable for real-time applications.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: WiFi-based Human Pose Estimation via Intermediate Pose Synthesis and Part Grouping.
abstract: As a non-contact and privacy-friendly sensing technology, WiFi-based human pose estimation holds significant potential for applications in intelligent surveillance and humancomputer interaction. However, existing methods still face two critical challenges. First, temporal sparsity caused by crossmodal alignment. To match low-sampling-rate visual labels, high-sampling-rate CSI signals are forced to be downsampled, leading to the loss of intermediate motion information. Second, the “negative transfer” effect caused by global feature sharing. Most models adopt a global feature sharing strategy, ignoring the relative independence of different body parts in motion patterns, which introduces interference from irrelevant parts and limits the precise modeling of highly dynamic joints. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel WiFi-based pose estimation framework that integrates temporal-interim pose synthesis with part-wise grouping modeling. In the temporal dimension, we design a temporally aware pose synthesis module that follows a “coarse-to-fine” generation strategy, explicitly inferring intermediate poses between adjacent frames in the feature space, thereby substantially enhancing temporal continuity. In the structural dimension, we introduce a data-driven part grouping strategy based on mutual information to automatically discover correlations among body parts, and employ a multi-branch network to model each part group independently, which mitigates negative transfer and strengthens local feature representations. Extensive experiments on the WiPose and MM-Fi datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches under the strict PCK@10 metric, achieving notable improvements especially on highly dynamic joints such as wrists and ankles. These results validate the effectiveness of our approach in continuous motion modeling and fine-grained WiFi-based pose estimation.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Noah: Tile-Level Interval Analysis for NPU Performance Modeling.
abstract: To meet the large-scale tensor computation requirements of LLMs, NPUs have become a mainstream architecture. Understanding their performance characteristics requires tools that can accurately capture complex hardware behaviors. However, existing approaches are limited by a trade-off: simulations enable accurate analysis but incur substantial cost, while analytical models offer speed but are too abstract to describe resource contention. To overcome these challenges, we propose Noah, a novel NPU analytical model. Noah models NPUs with a custom AI accelerator command ISA and reconstructs kernel execution as a pipelined interaction among compute, memory, and communication components. To improve fidelity, we explicitly model overlap behavior and major runtime stalls. For complex microarchitectural effects that are difficult to describe analytically, Noah incorporates a lightweight neural network. The proposed framework aims to provide an efficient and extensible approach for NPU performance modeling and early-stage design exploration.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SpecNet-Agent: Network-Aware Speculation Control for QoS in Agentic Generative AI Services.
abstract: Agentic generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) services increasingly process user requests as dynamic workflows that combine planning, retrieval, tool use, code execution, judging, and summarization, creating dependency-sensitive network transfers rather than a single model call. Existing quality of service (QoS) mechanisms are insufficient because flow scheduling, tenant fairness, static priorities, and coflow abstractions cannot reliably separate workflow-blocking traffic from cancelable or quality-elastic speculative branches. This paper presents SpecNetAgent, a runtime-network feedback framework that collects workflow hints, classifies traffic by probabilistic criticality, monitors congestion telemetry, and applies a safeguarded contextual-bandit controller to adjust retrieval width, agent parallelism, speculation budget, and background synchronization before traffic enters deployable QoS queues. The evaluation uses replay inputs derived from real-world agent execution logs, covering 1,237 workflows across retrieval-augmented generation question answering (RAG-QA), coding-agent, research-agent, and multi-agent debate templates under light, medium, and heavy loads. Under heavy load, SpecNet-Agent reduces p99 workflow latency to 192.93 time units, improving by 94.3% over first-in, firstout (FIFO), 89.9% over static priority, and 24.7% over criticalpath-only scheduling. It lowers deadline misses to 1.0% and cuts wasted speculative bytes by 76.2% over FIFO. Unlike aggressive rule-based feedback, it preserves a retained-speculation quality proxy of 0.967. These results demonstrate a practical contribution: network-aware source-side speculation control for improving QoS in agentic GenAI services.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Learning from Experience: Real-time and Efficient Network Measurement on Programmable Switches.
abstract: Sketches are one of the most efficient methods for network measurement. Some learning-based methods have addressed the issue of traditional sketches relying on a single assumption. However, due to the complexity of learning-based models, they can only be deployed on resource-rich servers. This necessitates frequent communication with the server when-ever the switch requires specific statistical information, thereby failing to satisfy the real-time decision-making requirements. Furthermore, the inability to obtain prior information in realtime hinders the execution of more complex downstream tasks. In this paper, we propose LFE, which simplifies the operations of learning-based models, making them compatible with programmable switches. LFE ensures the transmission of information within the switch, thereby supporting more complex realtime tasks. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that after optimization by LFE, the five commonly used sketches achieve an average reduction in AAE by 13.83% and an average reduction in ARE by 14.67%, with only a 4.56% reduction in throughput. The implementation is available at the repository1.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Multi-View Flow Representation and Relation Graph Modeling for Network Traffic Classification.
abstract: The widespread deployment of encryption protocols has fundamentally reduced payload visibility in network traffic, posing significant challenges to network behavior inference systems (e.g. Network Intrusion Detection System, NIDS) based solely on packet contents. Existing approaches often depend on coarse-grained flow-level statistics or isolated protocol metadata, which limits their ability to capture fine-grained TCP/IP packet sequences within individual flows as well as interaction patterns across multiple flows. From passive traffic measurements, we observe that an encrypted client–server communication typically spans multiple protocol stages, including domain name resolution, TLS handshake, and encrypted payload transmission. Additionally, complex network behaviors are often manifested through a sequence of correlated five-tuple flows rather than a single flow. To address these challenges, we propose a robust network behavior modeling framework, MV-FlowGraph, which characterizes encrypted traffic by jointly modeling multi-view intra-flow features and temporal inter-flow dependencies. Specifically, MV-FlowGraph consists of three key components: (1) a flow-level feature extraction and representation module that leverages server-side domain features recovered from plaintext DNS traffic, TLS handshake metadata, and TCP/IP packet transmission sequences; (2) a flow relation graph module that builds application-level flow graphs to capture inter-flow concurrency and sequential dependencies; and (3) a multi-view fusion module that employs BERT, autoencoders, and Graph Attention Networks to jointly model multi-view intra-flow features and temporal inter-flow features. Extensive experimental results verify that MV-FlowGraph out-performs state-of-the-art methods (e.g., AppScanner, FS-Net, and FG-Net) in detecting network anomalies targeting online services.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: MAS-CP: Multi-Agent Communication Prediction for Distributed Deep Neural Network Training.
abstract: Predicting all-reduce communication latency in distributed deep neural network (DNN) training is challenging because latency depends on both shared network state and per-worker program behavior. Existing approaches rely on monolithic predictors with fixed architectures, making them brittle across models and cluster sizes. We propose MAS-CP, a multi-agent framework with Locator, Analyzer, Predictor, and Verifier agents plus an orchestrator and RAG memory. On realworld BERT/GPT-2 traces and simulated multi-worker clusters with worker counts $W=2,4,8,16$, MAS-CP reduces MAE by $\mathbf{3. 6 \% - 6. 1 \%}$ over the best fixed-configuration baselines, with a closed-loop verification mechanism that automatically triggers re-prediction when errors exceed a dynamic threshold.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Heterogeneous Tasks Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing: A Federated Meta Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach.
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) supports latency-sensitive vehicular applications by offloading computation-intensive tasks to nearby edge servers. However, heterogeneous directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks with complex dependencies make task offloading and resource allocation highly challenging, while distributed MEC deployment introduces privacy concerns. In this paper, we propose FedMAGS, a federated meta deep reinforcement learning framework with GAT-Seq2Seq modeling for heterogeneous task offloading in VEC systems. The proposed framework combines Graph Attention Networks for dependency-aware DAG representation, Seq2Seq-based structured offloading decisions, and federated meta-learning for fast adaptation across distributed MEC servers without sharing raw data. Simulation results show that FedMAGS achieves faster convergence, lower execution delay, and better scalability than existing baselines while preserving data privacy in dynamic VEC environments.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: REACT: Toward Real-Time, End-to-End, Adaptive Cross-Layer Restoration for IP-Over-Optical Networks.
abstract: The resilience of optical networks is challenged by frequent fiber cuts. Jointly optimizing optical-layer rerouting and IP-layer traffic allocation yields optimal recovery, but solving the Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is prohibitively slow for real-time operation. Precomputation-based frameworks address this by generating recovery plans for highprobability failure scenarios, yet the number of possible failure patterns grows exponentially with network size, leaving numerous unforeseen cases unprotected. Recently, ML-based optical-layer restoration techniques are introduced to handle missed scenarios, but IP-layer recovery remains a bottleneck, limiting real-time responsiveness. To bridge this gap, this paper presents REACT, a responsive learning framework that enables real-time, joint optical and IP-layer restoration. REACT operates through two tightlyintegrated components: (i) an optical-layer restoration module that employs Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to swiftly generate feasible Routing and Wavelength Assignment (RWA) plans, and (ii) an IP-layer recovery module built upon a two-stage architecture: an initial traffic generation layer that transfers the network features into preliminary allocations, and a self-correction adjustment layer that refines these allocations using network metrics generated by the initial allocation. Evaluations on real-world topologies demonstrate that REACT achieves 95–99% of the optimal restoration throughput while delivering a speedup of over 19–3761$\times$ compared with other state-of-the-art (SOTA) cross-layer restoration schemes.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Dynamic Malicious Encrypted Traffic Detection via Temporal Knowledge Graph in Cloud-Edge Networks.
abstract: Traditional centralized security is inadequate for Cloud-Edge Networks, where massive distributed traffic and widespread protocol encryption create severe security blind spots. Continuous monitoring of network traffic is essential to identify malicious encrypted activities such as lateral movement and zero-day attacks. Existing graph-based detection methods typically model network flows as static graphs, which fail to capture the temporal dynamics of traffic patterns and face severe scalability bottlenecks when processing massive streaming data at resource-constrained edge nodes. Furthermore, supervised models heavily rely on exhaustive labeled datasets that are impractical to maintain in highly dynamic environments. To address these limitations, we propose TKG-ETA, a self-supervised Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) neural network equipped with an adaptive sketch mechanism for dynamic Encrypted Traffic Analysis in cloud-edge networks. We utilize a dynamically configurable sketch algorithm to efficiently compress and extract multi-dimensional statistical features from massive streaming traffic with minimal memory overhead, entirely bypassing payload inspection. These features are continuously transformed into a lightweight streaming TKG to model the fine-grained communication relations among network entities over time. Based on this temporal structure, we design a self-supervised time-aware message-passing mechanism to autonomously learn the evolutionary trajectories of normal encrypted traffic patterns without manual annotations. By capturing structural and temporal deviations, the proposed model accurately identifies malicious encrypted traffic. Extensive experiments on real-world network traffic datasets demonstrate that TKG-ETA achieves superior detection accuracy with an weighted F1 score exceeding 96% while maintaining the high throughput and low resource overhead imperative for cloud-edge collaborative deployment.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: HeraClass: Towards Open-World Network Flow Classification via Traffic-Language Mapping.
abstract: Network traffic classification in open-world settings, where applications evolve dynamically and labeled data is limited, remains an important unsolved problem. Existing techniques designed for static closed-world scenarios struggle when faced with shifting traffic patterns and categories. In this work, we formulate open-world flow classification (OWFC) as a crossmodal translation problem and identify four key challenges: (1) bridging the modality gap between traffic data and class labels, (2) discovering novel unknown classes at run-time, (3) learning representations for complex traffic features, and (4) rapidly adapting to new environments. To address these challenges, we propose HeraClass, a novel OWFC system that models temporal and categorical traffic features separately and learns them automatically, and maps traffic to a semantic language space to align known flows and their class labels, while making unknown flows depart from known class labels and thus maintaining low confidence to identify them as known ones. HeraClass supports real-time classification and can efficiently adapt to new environments using low-rank adaptation. Testbed experiments demonstrate HeraClass’s strong performance on both standard benchmarks and open-world scenarios, outperforming state-ofthe-art baselines by $\mathbf{1 2 0. 1 0 \%}$ on average for OWFC. We opensource pre-trained models, datasets, and implementation code to facilitate future research1.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CANListener: A Lightweight and Adaptive Intrusion Detection System for In-vehicle CAN Bus.
abstract: Controller Area Network (CAN) bus is the core communication backbone in modern vehicles, responsible for connecting Electronic Control Units (ECUs) and coordinating real-time in-vehicle operations. However, it is intrinsically without built-in security mechanisms. Existing works proposed Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) to protect CAN bus, ranging from rulebased to machine learning and deep learning-based methods. But most of them either require significant labeled samples or computational resources, or they suffer from severe detection performance degradation. Toward this end, this paper proposes CANListener, a lightweight and adaptive IDS for in-vehicle CAN bus. CANListener first employs a Reinforced Active Learning (RAL)-based method to train detection models with minimal but valuable labeled samples, enabling label-effective but accurate learning. Then, it integrates a Reinforcement Learning (RL)gated two-stage framework to dynamically allocate computational resources by routing inputs between lightweight and deep expert ensembles. Experimental results on real automotive datasets demonstrate that CANListener can achieve strong detection performance (99.48% TPR, 0.01% FPR) using only 1% labeled data, while maintaining real-time detection with an average CPU usage of 4.5% under hardware deployment.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CDWF: Few-Shot Learning for Cross-Domain Multi-Tab Website Fingerprinting.
abstract: Website fingerprinting attacks allow an eavesdropper to determine which websites a user is visiting by analyzing metadata from encrypted traffic, thereby posing a significant threat to online privacy. Most current methods rely on the assumption that a user visits only a single webpage at a time, which fails to account for the prevalence of multi-tab browsing in realistic scenarios. In such environments, traffic from multiple websites is interleaved, and practical attacks are further hindered by the scarcity of target-domain data, which limits the training efficacy and generalization of conventional models. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CDWF, a cross-domain few-shot website fingerprinting framework for multi-tab settings. The framework utilizes a three-stage progressive learning pipeline. First, traffic-augmented pre-training on public datasets extracts generalizable traffic representations through contrastive learning with diverse packet-level perturbations. Next, adversarial domain adaptation to align feature distributions between the source and target domains. Finally, few-shot target adaptation using a minimal set of target-domain samples and their augmented versions for rapid deployment. Experimental results demonstrate that CDWF significantly outperforms existing baselines in closed-world, open-world, and various defense scenarios. CDWF maintains superior robustness and recognition accuracy even when the number of tabs is unknown and under strong defensive conditions. This work provides an effective solution for practical website fingerprinting attacks in environments with limited data and constrained resources.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: MACH: A Matrix-Accelerated Classifier for High-throughput Packet Processing on GPUs.
abstract: Packet classification is a core function in modern network systems. While learning-based methods demonstrate promising throughput on large-scale rulesets, existing indices fail to effectively exploit GPU parallelism. Specifically, the hierarchical structure of recursive models creates irregular control flow patterns, leading to branch divergence and non-coalesced memory accesses that degrade throughput at scale. To address this limitation, we propose MACH, a throughput-oriented packet classification framework. MACH utilizes a unified neural network trained on multi-dimensional features to ensure complete rule coverage without rule duplication. By adopting a semi-structured design that couples the neural model with a tuple space, the framework reduces model complexity and supports efficient dynamic updates. Crucially, this architecture transforms irregular rule lookups into dense matrix operations, aligning classification tasks with GPU computation primitives. A CPU-GPU hybrid streaming pipeline is further implemented to maximize aggregate batch throughput. Evaluations on rulesets with 512k entries demonstrate that MACH achieves 12.19x and 9.37x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art learning-based baselines, NuevoMatch and NeuTree, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Adaptive Multi-Path Mamba Knowledge Distillation Framework for Industrial Defect Detection.
abstract: Industrial defect detection (IDD) plays a vital role in intelligent manufacturing. In practical industrial environments, defects are often small-scale, low-contrast, and morphologically complex, posing stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements. Real-time edge deployment demands a careful balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency; however, existing methods remain constrained by the inherent accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. To address this challenge, we propose a deployment-oriented Multi-Path Mamba-in-Mamba Knowledge Distillation framework (MPMiM-KD), designed to preserve strong detection capability while minimizing inference overhead. Specifically, a multi-path Mamba teacher network is constructed to capture multi-scale defect patterns through parallel branches with diverse receptive fields, providing enriched supervisory signals during training. The teacher model is used exclusively for knowledge transfer and does not increase deployment complexity. An adaptive distillation strategy with dynamic temperature control is further introduced to efficiently transfer discriminative knowledge to a compact student network. In addition, cross-path attention enables intermediate feature alignment, enhancing robustness to complex defect patterns without incurring additional inference cost. Experimental results on the Real-IAD dataset demonstrate that MPMiM-KD improves AUROC by 2.4% over the previous state-of-the-art while reducing model parameters by 30.3% and computational cost by 17.7%, indicating its potential for efficient industrial defect detection under resource-constrained deployment scenarios.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Few-Packet Traffic Classification under Dynamic Network Conditions.
abstract: Few-packet traffic classification is essential for network management and security monitoring but faces severe instability under dynamic network conditions. Packet loss and reordering cause inconsistent partial observations of the same flow, degrading both accuracy and reliability. We identify this observation inconsistency as a fundamental challenge and model it through the Partial Observation Consistency (POC). Further, we propose POC-FPC, a framework that learns consistent representations across multiple partial views. POC-FPC comprises three novel components: a multi-view generator simulating packet loss and reordering, an order-relaxed set-based flow encoder that reduces sensitivity to packet order, and a two-level consistency mechanism that aligns representations and predictions only on overlapping packet subsets. This avoids noise supervision from unobservable components. Finally, our experiments on multiple datasets show that POC-FPC improves accuracy up to 41.76% and prediction stability up to 25.6% over state-ofthe-art solutions, demonstrating robust few-packet classification under realistic network perturbations.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ALCHEMY: Reusing Congestion Control Wisdom for Adaptive QUIC Transport.
abstract: No single congestion control (CC) algorithm performs well across heterogeneous and time-varying network conditions. While loss-based, delay-based, and hybrid designs excel in specific regimes, they degrade outside them. Conversely, fully learned CC approaches offer adaptability but raise concerns regarding interpretability and deployment safety. Consequently, today’s systems lack a robust mechanism to dynamically select the optimal strategy during an active connection. We address this gap with ALCHEMY, a framework that enables adaptive CC selection in QUIC. ALCHEMY introduces a state-preserving midstream switching mechanism that allows CC algorithms to be safely changed within an ongoing connection without triggering slow-start resets or control instability. Building on this capability, ALCHEMY employs an offline-trained deep reinforcement learning policy to select the most appropriate expert algorithm at runtime using cross-layer transport signals. Rather than replacing existing CC logic, ALCHEMY orchestrates established heuristics, leveraging their complementary strengths. Implemented in a high-fidelity emulated QUIC stack and evaluated across 26 diverse network scenarios, ALCHEMY demonstrates superior adaptability compared to static baselines. It improves the scenario-wise winning rate by approximately 29% relative to the best-performing individual heuristic CC algorithm. Here, winning rate denotes the frequency of achieving the highest composite throughput–delay score among all evaluated schemes. Unlike static algorithms that are bound to a fixed design envelope, ALCHEMY consistently maintains near-optimal throughput-delay trade-offs across heterogeneous and volatile regimes.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: HawkEye: Hierarchical Intent Inference for Critical Targets on Edge-Cloud Co-Assisted UAVs.
abstract: Urban safety inspection by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) requires accurate and trustworthy recognition of target intent, yet existing efforts face a dual dilemma: the system level struggles to handle limited UAV arithmetic and high cloud transmission latency, and the algorithmic level is susceptible to trajectory noise and unreliable “black-box” decisions. To this end, we propose HawkEye, a data-model dual-driven two-stage intent inference framework. Adopting an edge-cloud collaboration paradigm, HawkEye handles UAV observations with two innovative breakthroughs. On the edge, to overcome the uncertainty of target motion, we replace traditional single-trajectory fitting strategies with an anchor-based statistical inference method for short-term intents. By fusing anchor classification with kinematic constraints and Bayesian-optimized adaptive fault-tolerant intervals, this method predicts physically feasible and noise-robust steering angles and trajectories within milliseconds, providing solid priors for the cloud. On the cloud, we tailor the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for long-term tactical-level intents. A domain knowledge base embedded with typical motion and interaction features is especially built, empowering Large Language Models (LLMs) to make high-accuracy, map-free, and logically traceable intent inference. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets show that HawkEye improves short-term accuracy to 88.5% with 61.5% latency reduction, and long-term accuracy by 19.4%, successfully balancing real-time response and reliable intent recognition.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: ChatGosen: A Network Configuration Synthesis Approach with Semantic-Computation Decoupling.
abstract: Network configuration synthesis aims to translate high-level configuration intent into concrete device-level configurations. Recent research has explored leveraging large language models (LLMs) for intent inference and configuration synthesis. However, configuration synthesis inherently requires deterministic topology analysis and protocol-parameter resolution, such as deriving OSPF link costs, BGP route preferences, or static-route next hops from topology constraints and intended forwarding behavior. These operations require explicit protocol semantics and cannot be reliably guaranteed by the probabilistic generation process of LLMs. We propose ChatGosen, a network configuration synthesis method based on semantic-computation decoupling. This approach separates intent inference from deterministic protocol-parameter resolution through a structured, vendor-independent intermediate representation (IR). The LLM handles intent reasoning, task decomposition, generation of device-level configuration subtasks, and final configuration file generation, while topology parsing and protocol-parameter resolution are processed by a deterministic protocol-parameter resolution module. We implemented a prototype system supporting static routing, OSPF, and BGP protocols. Testing on the Topology Zoo real-world network topology dataset demonstrated ChatGosen achieves fully correct routing forwarding configurations in single-intent scenarios across 64-router topologies, with accuracy exceeding 85% in multi-intent scenarios. The synthesis process completes in mere minutes, proving that semantic-computation decoupling provides a practical and scalable foundation for network-wide configuration synthesis.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: GBNN: In-Network Gradient Boosting Neural Network.
abstract: In-network intelligence offloads machine learning models to programmable network devices for line-rate packet classification and improved quality of service (QoS). However, existing lightweight models are often limited in fine-grained classification, while Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs), though accurate for complex traffic classification tasks, are difficult to deploy in network due to resource constraints, sequential inference latency, and disruptive runtime updates. To address these challenges, we propose GBNN, an in-network GBDTequivalent model that replaces GBDT leaf nodes with Binary Neural Networks (BNNs). GBNN preserves the boosting structure of GBDTs while leveraging compact bitwise BNN inference to reduce resource consumption and latency. Moreover, its BNNbased design enables a shadow model mechanism for nondisruptive runtime updates without device reboot. Experiments on a Raspberry Pi-based testbed show that GBNN achieves accuracy comparable to GBDT, while reducing CPU usage by 82.5% and inference latency by over $7.1 \times$.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CBDDoSCLIP: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for Carpet-Bombing DDoS Attack Detection.
abstract: Carpet-bombing DDoS spreads low-rate traffic across many IPs within a /24 subnet, keeping per-host volume within normal ranges and defeating threshold-based detectors. CBDDoSCLIP converts backbone traffic into time–destination-IP CB Images and aligns them with CLIP text for multimodal detection at low trainable-parameter cost. Contributions: (i) CB Images with time binning and IP ordering for simultaneous and sequential patterns; (ii) dual visual encoder, DDoSAdapter residual adaptation, and candidate prompt selection; (iii) training only adapter and projection layers with frozen encoders (~1M parameters). On CICDDoS2019/CICIDS2017 splits and a 100k-sample backbone test set, CBDDoSCLIP matches full fine-tuning accuracy at lower parameter and training cost.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: DMKG: DDoS Defense Enhanced by Multimodal Knowledge Graph Data.
abstract: Modern DDoS attacks increasingly employ multivector combinations, low-rate behaviors, and traffic mimicry to evade detection. Existing deep learning-based defenses efficiently analyze low-level telemetry but usually act as semantic black boxes without explicit mitigation logic. Conversely, Large Language Model (LLM)-based defense systems frequently hallucinate when detached from factual traffic evidence and domain-specific causal constraints. To bridge this gap, we propose DMKG, a multimodal knowledge graph-driven DDoS defense framework that connects low-level traffic evidence with high-level defense knowledge. DMKG constructs a DDoS-specific KG from expert manuals, system alerts, and PCAP-derived evidence, and designs PCAPBERT to anchor PCAP traffic to symbolic attack categories through metric learning. Based on the generated factual traffic summaries, we further develop DDoSRAG to enforce explicit meta-path constraints and reconstruct complete attack-defense causal chains, grounding LLM generation in structured expert logic. Evaluations on a unified benchmark built from CICIDS2017 and CICDDoS2019 demonstrate that DMKG achieves strong performance in Defensive Strategy Recommendation, Context-aware Attack Chain Completion, and Causal Reasoning Explainability. The quantitative results further show that DMKG consistently outperforms pure LLM and standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation baselines.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Prediction-Based Adaptive Edge Caching Update Strategy for the Internet of Vehicles.
abstract: The integration of IoV and MEC leads to a surge in delay-sensitive content requests. In viaduct scenarios, 3D structures cause frequent LOS/NLOS transitions, posing challenges to traditional edge caching. This paper presents an edge intelligencebased adaptive caching framework with LSTM popularity prediction and DQN decision-making. Experiments on real-world SUMO trajectories show that our method achieves 77.35% cache hit ratio and 31.2 ms average latency, which outperforms baseline schemes by up to $\mathbf{6. 0 6 \%}$ and $\mathbf{1 1. 4 \%}$, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Minimizing the Delay Disparity for Cross-Region Virtual Reality Gaming in Satellite Edge Computing.
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) gaming is one of the delay-sensitive services that require guaranteeing ultra-low and fair delay experience for their users. A conventional VR gaming service is hosted in ground data centers and only admits players from the same geographical region to guarantee a fair experienced delay of players. Cross-region VR gaming in such service deployments leads to large delay disparity among players in different regions, since players in different regions have varying ground network accessibility. In contrast, satellite edge computing (SEC) that integrates satellite communication and edge computing bypasses ground network barriers, making it the only option for cross-region VR gaming. In this paper, we investigate a fundamental problem of multi-player cross-region VR gaming with the aim of guaranteeing a fair gaming experience for players. We first formulate an optimization problem of the delay disparity minimization problem for a multi-player cross-region VR gaming service in an SEC network. We propose an approximation algorithm with an approximation ratio by leveraging a non-trivial transformation into the capacitated K-center problem. We also consider the scenario where the actions of players in VR gaming services are bursty and uncertain, by formulating the online delay disparity minimization problem for multiple cross-region VR gaming services with bursty player actions in an SEC network. We devise an online learning algorithm with a bounded regret by adopting a multi-armed bandit method. We finally evaluate the algorithm performance via extensive simulations based on real satellite network topologies generated by Ansys Systems Tool Kit (STK). Results show that our algorithms outperform their counterparts by achieving $\mathbf{2 5. 6 \%}$ lower the delay disparity.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Joint Optimization of MEC Offloading and Traffic Signal Control via Diffusion-based Hierarchical DRL.
abstract: The rapid proliferation of vehicular applications has intensified the demand for Mobile Edge Computing (MEC). Existing resource management strategies typically treat Traffic Signal Control (TSC) as a static environmental constraint, ignoring the coupling effect between vehicles’ mobility and computational power. In this paper, we propose Joint Optimization via Diffusion-based Hierarchical DRL (JO-DHD) to synergize active traffic regulation with task offloading. Specifically, we design a hierarchical control mechanism in which the high-level agent manipulates traffic signals to form ad hoc vehicular computing clusters during high-load periods, thereby converting temporary vehicle aggregation into usable computational capacity. To address the resulting high-dimensional hybrid action space, we introduce a conditional diffusion-based actor that uses a conditional diffusion process for policy generation. Extensive experiments show that JO-DHD outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 9.8% in composite performance, achieving an optimal trade-off between mobility efficiency and computational latency.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RGB: Resource Graph Base for Integrating Tri-Elements in Computing Power Networks.
abstract: Intelligent scheduling is pivotal for unlocking the service potential of Computing Power Networks (CPNs), which requires joint optimization of computing power, algorithms, and data. Analogous to image creation which relies on the blending of primary colors, Quality of Service (QoS) is not dictated by any single element but rather by the synergistic alignment of these three elements. However, existing methods often fail to characterize such collaborative effects, struggling to capture the cross-element dependencies and their impact on scheduling decisions. To address these limitations, we propose RGB-Painter, a Resource Graph-Based scheduling framework that leverages the synergistic interplay among these elements for collaborationaware scheduling in CPNs. Specifically, we construct a trielement resource graph to integrate the three elements and employ graph neural networks to learn fused representations of their dynamic couplings. We then incorporate these embeddings into a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning module equipped with an action masking mechanism, enabling efficient distributed scheduling decision-making. Simulation results demonstrate that RGB-Painter reduces the average task completion time by 5.48%-42.58% compared with multiple baselines, validating its efficacy for deployment in real-world CPNs.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification.
abstract: Pre-trained models operating directly on raw bytes have achieved promising performance in encrypted network traffic classification (NTC), but often suffer from shortcut learning-relying on spurious correlations that fail to generalize to real-world data. Existing solutions rely on model-specific interpretation, lacking adaptability across architectures and deployment scenarios. We propose BiasSeeker, the first semiautomated, model-agnostic and data-driven framework for detecting dataset-specific shortcut features in encrypted traffic. By performing statistical correlation analysis directly on raw binary traffic, BiasSeeker identifies spurious or environmententangled features independent of any classifier. We further introduce a systematic categorization and apply category-specific validation strategies that reduce bias while preserving meaningful information. Evaluations on 19 public datasets across three NTC tasks demonstrate BiasSeeker’s effectiveness, raising awareness that feature selection should be an intentional, scenario-sensitive step prior to model training.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: SE-STGAE: A Shapelet-Enhanced Spatiotemporal Graph Autoencoder for Early Anomaly Detection.
abstract: Early anomaly detection in networked sensing is crucial for maintaining the Quality of Service (QoS), especially under strict False Positive Rate (FPR) budgets where alarms must be early and reliable. Existing methods typically learn normal spatiotemporal patterns from multi-node sensing streams and raise alarms using reconstruction deviations in a one-class manner. However, in real freeway monitoring, anomalies exhibit complex spatiotemporal propagation and the early anomaly signals are sparse. Meanwhile, traffic streams contain diverse normal fluctuations that may look abnormal, making them hard to distinguish from real incidents. Together, these factors make anomaly propagation hard to capture under strict low-FPR earlywarning settings. To address these challenges, we propose SE-STGAE, a shapelet-enhanced spatiotemporal graph autoencoder. It first uses shapelets to extract localized segment-level precursors, then integrates temporal precursors with propagationaware spatial dependencies to improve robustness to normal fluctuations, and finally applies a tail-emphasized Top-K scoring rule with pure-normal calibration for reliable early alarming. Extensive experiments on real-world freeway datasets show consistent gains over state-of-the-art baselines across datasets and FPR budgets, delivering earlier detection with localized evidence.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Ensuring QoS Stability in Dynamic WANs through Selectively Optimized Range Routing.
abstract: Network traffic volatility frequently causes severe Quality of Service (QoS) degradation. Preventing this degradation requires Traffic Engineering (TE) solutions that maintain robustness against dynamic traffic shifts, preserve scalability for computational efficiency, and operate effectively with limited historical data. However, existing TE solutions fail to satisfy these three conditions simultaneously. Conventional mathematical model-based solutions struggle to balance between scalability and resilience to traffic variations. While recent deep learningbased solutions demonstrate strong scalability and robustness, their performance depends heavily on massive datasets of Traffic Matrices (TMs). To resolve these limitations and guarantee QoS, we propose Selectively Optimized Range Routing (SORR) to satisfy all three TE requirements through two core schemes. First, SORR reduces the dependence on massive historical TMs by employing a data-model hybrid architecture that synergistically combines deep reinforcement learning with established mathematical routing models. Second, it leverages a hierarchical collaborative optimization strategy that distributes TE tasks across different routing models according to their specific operational roles, ensuring both high scalability and resilience. Evaluations using public datasets and real traffic traces confirm that SORR delivers good performance using as few as 96 TMs. Compared to existing solutions, SORR improves the worst-case performance by 79% while conceding only a 2% reduction in median-case performance.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: CoPT: Collaborative Machine-Learning-Based Mechanism for Adaptive Congestion Control Parameter Tuning in Data Center Networks.
abstract: As the types and scale of applications supported by data center networks continue to expand, network traffic characteristics are becoming increasingly complex, exhibiting high dynamism and heterogeneity in both time and space dimensions. Efficient congestion control technology is crucial to optimizing network performance. Adaptive adjustment mechanisms for congestion control parameters based on distributed switches and centralized controllers often exhibit limitations when handling complex and changing traffic characteristics, resulting in poor network performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CoPT, a Collaborative machine-learningbased mechanism for adaptive congestion control Parameter Tuning in data center networks. This mechanism uses a network performance model in the centralized controller to predict portlevel ECN parameters for global network traffic and sends the predictions as “guidance” to the switch control plane. A guided-reinforcement-learning-based agent is deployed on the distributed switch ports. This agent, combined with local traffic characteristics and global ECN parameters, “guides” the selection of optimal parameters, effectively adapting to various complex traffic characteristics and significantly improving network performance. Experimental results show that, under various traffic scenarios, CoPT significantly outperforms both distributed-based and centralized-based methods in terms of flow completion time (FCT) and reduction of average queue length.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Beyond Random Probing: Intelligent IPv6 Discovery via Ensemble Learning and Contextual Expansion.
abstract: The vast IPv6 address space renders exhaustive scanning computationally infeasible. We present DeepScan6, a hybrid discovery framework integrating three components: ensemble-based seed preprocessing, a novel Context Expansion (CEX) mechanism, and a tolerance-based incremental learning module. CEX performs prefix-by-prefix IID sequence analysis within individual /64 prefixes and generates candidates through prioritized interpolation and extrapolation. The incremental learning module selectively incorporates newly discovered addresses via lightweight iterative updates, enabling self-improvement across rounds without full retraining. DeepScan6 achieves a 75-77% hit rate on heterogeneous seed sets, outperforming nine baseline methods by 22.1-72.1%. Deployed at scale, it yields 10,139,214 new active addresses beyond the IPv6Hitlist across 1,232 ASes in 92 countries. Measurement reveals severe address concentration (top-3 ASes: 49.89%), extreme subnet sparsity (86.8% of /64 subnets contain one address), 20.87% high-risk IID patterns, and 42.01% of HTTPS-responsive addresses simultaneously exposing HTTP.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: GCA-BULF: A Bottom-Up Framework for Short-Term Load Forecasting Using Grouped Critical Appliances.
abstract: With the rise of time-of-use and tiered electricity pricing, energy consumers are encouraged to adopt peak-shifting strategies by automatically controlling high-power appliances. These help lower energy costs while enhancing the power grid's stability. To support such energy management with high resilience and responsiveness, reliable short-term load forecasting (STLF) plays a critical role. STLF predicts electricity consumption over time horizons ranging from minutes to days, using historical data, temporal patterns, and contextual factors. Traditional top-down forecasting methods struggle to capture the complex consumption patterns of diverse and mixed appliance loads. Although bottom-up methods improve forecasting accuracy by integrating appliance-level data, monitoring all appliances is costly, and many do not meaningfully impact total load prediction. Therefore, we propose GCA-BULF, a bottom-up short-term load forecasting framework based on grouped critical appliances, supported by three key designs. First, the Critical Appliance Filtering module ranks appliances according to their power consumption, switching frequency, and usage pattern periodicity, and identifies critical ones through iterative load decomposition. Next, the Related Appliance Grouping module clusters these appliances based on spatial and temporal correlations for group-level forecasting. Finally, the Collaborative Load Forecasting module refines the total load prediction by combining multiple group-level forecasts. We evaluate GCA-BULF on residential and office building load forecasting tasks. Experimental results reveal that GCA-BULF improves hourly total load forecasting by 20.85%-57.88% compared to existing top-down methods and by 33.03%-92.48% compared to bottom-up methods.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: An Adaptive Multi-Metric Forwarding Strategy for Vehicular Named Data Networking with Hybrid Contention and Opportunistic Delivery.
abstract: Vehicular Named Data Networking (VNDN) requires robust Quality of Service (QoS) for intelligent transportation. However, broadcast storms and network partitions often hinder performance. This paper proposes an Adaptive Multi-Metric Contention and Opportunistic Forwarding (AMCOF) strategy. It uses a lightweight Q-learning agent to tune metric weights based on local density dynamically. The strategy integrates Top-K truncation and a Store-Carry-Forward (SCF) mechanism to handle diverse environments. Simulation results show that AMCOF improves delivery reliability and network efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: RAPIDS: Reliable Adaptive Priority-based Intelligent Delivery Streaming for Enhanced Error Resilience in Real-time Video.
abstract: Real-time video streaming (RVS) has become the Internet’s dominant application, supporting latency-critical services from telemedicine to remote collaboration. However, stringent latency requirements force RVS systems to rely on UDP-based transport that tolerates packet loss, creating reliability challenges. Packet loss, whether from congestion or transmission errors, creates two irreconcilable failure modes: if corrupted reference frames are displayed, prediction errors propagate through all dependent frames, causing severe visual degradation; if packets are retransmitted aggressively, latency accumulates beyond real-time tolerances. This dilemma cannot be resolved within either layer independently: transport-layer mechanisms like retransmission or FEC exacerbate congestion, while codec-layer solutions like bitrate reduction degrade visual quality.We present RAPIDS, a codec-transport co-design that resolves this impasse through dynamic dependency restructuring. RAPIDS employs a deep reinforcement learning controller to adaptively designate frames as reference or non-reference based on real-time network conditions, effectively decoupling frame importance from encoding structure. This semantic information guides a partially reliable QUIC transport to implement differentiated protection: critical reference frames receive guaranteed delivery via retransmission, while non-reference frames can be proactively discarded under congestion to bound latency. Extensive evaluation on 1000+ real-world network traces demonstrates 28-50% QoS improvement over WebRTC, Salsify, and SODA, with a 4-5× faster error recovery during traffic bursts and network outages.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: StreamDuet: Bandwidth Efficient Multi-Drone Video Analytics with Iterative Streaming.
abstract: Drone video analytics is widely applied across various smart city services, including traffic monitoring, industrial inspection, and crowd anomaly detection. However, a single drone often suffers from occlusions and poor viewing angles, leading to significant accuracy reduction. Multi-drone systems capture videos from multiple perspectives, which enhance the accuracy by integrating complementary information from different fields of view (FoVs). Despite this advantage, limited bandwidth in drone networks makes it challenging to transmit high-resolution videos efficiently. This paper introduces StreamDuet, a system designed to enable high-accuracy and low-bandwidth video analytics in multi-drone systems. To this end, it addresses key challenges by leveraging three core components: 1) a Dynamic FoV Region of Interest (RoI) Prediction that quickly and accurately identifies accuracy-beneficial regions in each video chunk and encodes only them into video streams, 2) a Spatio-Temporal Inference Results Sharing mechanism that effectively manages and shares inference results across FoVs and continuous frames among multiple drones, and 3) a Temporal Robust Inference Results Reuse module that predicts current frame results by reusing inferences from previous frames within a single drone. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that StreamDuet improves $\mathbf{8}-\mathbf{4 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$ accuracy and reduces 28-61% bandwidth consumption compared to the state-of-the-art systems.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service

title: Speak Your Network: Automated Network Emulation Construction with Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Orchestration.
abstract: Network research often relies on high fidelity emulation, but constructing greenfield environments still requires substantial manual effort. LLM agents face a gap between intent and implementation: long contexts, weak validation, and uniform model use make it difficult to translate intent into working emulator state. We present Nice, a closed-loop multi-agent framework that constructs greenfield emulations from natural language intents. Nice combines a hierarchical supervisor and worker architecture with context isolation, closed-loop verification for state grounding and self-healing, dual-layer experience memory, and adaptive LLM routing. On a 30-task benchmark, Nice increases success rate from 3.3% to 90.0%, reduces average model cost from ${\$}$0.045 to ${\$}$0.034 per task relative to the variant without routing, and improves first pass rate from 46.7% to 76.7%.
conference_title: IEEE/ACM International Workshop on Quality of Service
